newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Tullow to progress Pakistan gas discovery.
newsitem.headline: Tullow to progress Pakistan gas discovery.

text.p: Tullow Oil Plc said on Monday it believed the Sara West gas discovery in Pakistan will be commercial and it intended to progress the development options with its partners and the authorities in Pakistan.

The Irish exploration group said in a statement that it had received a technical report on the economic feasibility of developing Sara West, which was discovered in September 1996 and flowed low quality gas at up to 25 mmscfd.

"The report examined the practicalities and economics of improving the combustible quality of the Sara West gas and as a result, Tullow now believes that the field will be commercial," the company said.
Tullow said development plans on its other Pakistani discoveries were continuing.

The company also said it had entered into an agreement with Addax Petroleum Ltd to acquire, subject to certain conditions and government approval, a 36 percent interest in Block C1-26 offshore Ivory Coast.

The block contains the Espoir Field which was discovered, developed and put on production by Phillips Petroleum for a number of years in the 1980s prior to their prematurely abandoning the area as a result of low oil prices, less favourable economic terms prevailing at that time and for certain strategic reasons, Tullow said.

"A technical and economic study for the re-development of the field is currently being carried out and Tullow and Addax are confident that the study will demonstrate the commercial viability of a re-development of the field," Tullow said.
The company also said it had entered into an agreement with Okland Oil Company and Rexwood Corporation, with a view to actively pursuing various oil and gas opportunities in Bangladesh.
Tullow has also been awarded, or made arrangements to farm-in to, a total of four exploration licences in India.
Three of these are onshore and one offshore and one contains a small commercial gas discovery that will commence production shortly.
In Egypt, Tullow has been awarded the North Abu Rudeis block on the eastern bank of the Gulf of Suez, as operator.
"This large oil play is in a highly prospective area and, following a seismic acquisitions programme which is due to commence shortly, a well is expected to be drilled later this year," Tullow said.

The company currently has a 60 percent interest in this licence but has concluded arrangements, subject to various approvals, to farm-out part of its interest prior to drilling, leaving Tullow with 33.33 percent.

In Britain, the West Firsby-6 development well was recently completed and is producing at an average rate in excess of 500 barrels of oil per day while the Kishma-1 discovery well in Syria has been supplemented by the successful appraisal well Kishma-2 which is currently being tested.

Tullow said it continues to make good progress in its discussions with the authorities and partners in relation to the development of the Mnazi Bay gas field and the establishment of a related integrated gas-to-power project in southern Tanzania.
"Discussions with a power industry partner are at an advanced state," Tullow said.
The company is also pursuing a number of other exploration and development initiatives in its core areas of interest including West Africa and the Indian sub-continent.
